question.leadin: Answer these questions about languages related to English.
question.text: The region of Flanders in Belgium is primarily home to speakers of this language, also spoken in Suriname and Aruba.
question.clue: People who were unable to pronounce the words "shield and friend" in this language were killed in a nighttime massacre just before the Battle of the Golden Spurs.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Netherlands, whose name literally means "low-lying countries"
swap.text: In 2020, the Dutch government announced it would no longer support using this name to refer to the Netherlands since this name only represents a region and former province within the Netherlands.
swap.clue: The "cod" and "hook" factions ensnared this county in a 15th-century succession dispute ended by a Burgundian invasion.

question.text: During the opening of World War I, Germany used the Schlieffen Plan, which called for an invasion of this nation led by King Albert I. The "Big Bertha" howitzer was used to destroy Forts Pontisse and Loncin in this country.
question.clue: This country's king surrendered it during World War II against the wishes of Pierlot, its prime minister.

swap.text: This Catholic nobleman led a group of like-minded politiques to ask Philip II to tolerate Protestantism in the Netherlands.
swap.answerHtml: William of Orange (accept William the Silent, prompt on William)
swap.clue: This man had an illegitimate son with Eva Elincx, and that son Justinus became the admiral who handed over the keys of Breda to Ambrogio Spinola.

question.text: The United Nations established a tribunal in this city to prosecute war criminals from former Yugoslavia. It is home to the International Court of Justice.
question.clue: In this city, the ICTY convicted Slobodan Milosevic of war crimes in a trial at this city's Peace Palace.

swap.leadin: Everyone knows the earth is flat, so why is it so hard to decide on a suitable map projection?
swap.text: This projection, created in 1569, uses straight longitude and latitude lines that make Greenland and Africa nearly the same size.
swap.clue: In 1569, this type of map projection was created by the namesake Flemish cartographer. A standard map projection, it is noted for distorting the size and shape of large objects, thus making Greenland look huge.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about a naval fleet commanded by the duke of Medonia Sodenia.
question.text: The Armada was assembled in response to this 1585 treaty which Elizabeth I signed. It provided English cavalry and solders to the Netherlands, and was signed in response to Philip's signing of the Treaty of Joinville.
question.clue: Following Philip II's signing of the Treaty of Joinville, Elizabeth agreed to this treaty with The Neatherlands which promised military and financial support with the goal of lifting the Siege of Antwerp.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Dutch Revolt.
swap.text: One of the Dutch side's most successful military leaders was this man, who led Dutch forces in the first quarter of the 1600s after the death of William the Silent.
swap.clue: This man used the alleged crime of raising of waargelder forces as an excuse to execute his the pro-Arminianism and pro-peace rival Johan van Oldenbarnevelt.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the violent history of Europe.
question.text: Organized by the Duke of Alba, this court in the Spanish Netherlands attempted to suppress Calvinism and tighten Spanish control over the Netherlands by enforcing the Tenth Penny tax.
question.answerHtml: Council of Blood [or Council of Troubles; or Raad Van Beroerten; or Bloedraad; or Tribunal de los Revoltosos; or Tribunal de Sangre; accept reasonable equivalents for "Council", such as "Court" ]
question.clue: This tribunal created by the Duke of Alba to deal with unrest in the early stages of the Dutch Revolt.

swap.text: Napoleon III denied a Hohenzollern prince with this name the chance to ascend to the Spanish throne, precipitating the Franco-Prussian War. A man with this name was crowned king of a new country after an 1830 revolution that broke out at an opera performance.
swap.clue: Atrocities committed under a king of this name were detailed in the Casement Report which included accounts of his Force Publique severing the limbs of workers who failed to meet rubber quotas.

question.leadin: According to the book The Bookshop of the World, during this period, 10 times more books were produced per capita than in France or Spain.
question.text: Name this period, also the subject of Simon Schama's The Embarrassment of Riches. This period's end is traditionally dated to the "Disaster Year" of 1672.
question.answerHtml: Dutch Golden Age [or Gouden Eeuw; or Netherlands Golden Age; or Dutch Miracle; prompt on Golden Age]

swap.text: After finding Livingstone, Stanley later worked as an agent for this Belgian king's International African Association. This king's agents committed numerous atrocities in his privately owned Congo Free State.
swap.clue: This man formed the Force Publique to enforce his rule in a certain area, but was criticized in the Casement Report, which detailed atrocities inflicted upon rubber harvesters.

question.leadin: After this meeting, Hugo Grotius was sentenced to life imprisonment, but escaped thanks to his mistress smuggling him out of prison in a book chest.
question.text: Name this 1618 to 1619 synod in the Netherlands convened to settle the Arminian controversy. This meeting saw disputes between the Arminians and followers of Franciscus Gomarus, as well as the condemnation of Johan von Oldenbarnevelt.
question.answerHtml: Synod of Dort [or Synod of Dordt or Synod of Dordrecht]
question.clue: Moderated by Bogerman, it set forth the doctrines of perseverance of saints, irresistible grace, total depravity, limited atonement, and unconditional election.

swap.text: Many Flemish nationalists point to this battle during Philip IV's invasion of Flanders as a point of pride. Robert D'Artois ("dar-TWAH") was killed in this 1302 battle, named for a piece of equipment that was found littered on the battlefield after.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [or Battle of Courtrai]
swap.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

question.text: This woman was the queen of the Netherlands during the war. She fled to Great Britain during the occupation and broadcast messages of inspiration to the Dutch resistance movement.

swap.leadin: This event began when attendees of Daniel Auber's opera La Muette de Portici joined Catholic rioters outside the theater doors after hearing the duet "Sacred Love of the Fatherland."
swap.text: Name this 1830 event led by Charles Rogier ("roh-zhee-AY"). The Ten Days' Campaign supported by William I failed to topple a monarch installed during this event.
swap.answerHtml: Belgian Revolution [or Révolution Belge; or Belgische Revolutie; or Belgische Opstand; or Belgische Omwenteling; prompt on Belgian independence]
swap.clue: Sparked by perceived anti-Catholic policies, it brought to power the widower of Princess Charlotte of Wales, who later arranged the marriage of his niece Victoria to his nephew Albert.

question.leadin: This city's first prince-bishop was the illustrious Notger, who had the Saint Lambert cathedral built.
question.text: Name this so-called "Athens of the North," if by "North" you mean "Belgium," whose greatest Renaissance ruler was Erard de la Marck.
question.clue: The strike of 1902, the second in a series of general strikes in Belgium, began when wildcat strikes broke out among miners in this province. This province faced a 1789 revolution called the Happy Revolution that restored the policies of Prince-Bishop Velbruck.

swap.leadin: The RAF and US Army Air Forces attempted to alleviate this event by organizing food drops termed Operation Manna and Operation Chowhound.
swap.text: Name this massive famine that took place in German-occupied Netherlands at the end of World War II.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a common theme, FTPE.
question.text: Though she had abdicated five years prior, this former Dutch monarch joined her daughter, Queen Juliana, in personally visiting victims of the 1953 Netherlands deluge. As the only surviving heir of William III, she eventually became the first titled queen of the Netherlands.

swap.leadin: This river names a World War II battle fought in October and November of 1944, which saw Canadian general Guy Simonds attempt to clear the namesake estuary for the Allies after the failure of Operation Market Garden.
swap.text: Name this roughly 350-kilometer long European river. Its banks are home to cities like Tournai, Cambrai, and Flushing.
